title: Chapter 104
content:
[Earlier this morning, Haewon Group CEO Kang Il-hyun appeared before the prosecution for questioning as a key witness. A massive press corps had been camped outside the Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office since dawn. Following the tragic incident, Haewon Group announced sweeping executive restructuring and personnel overhauls to restore public trust and overhaul corporate governance.]

Behind the anchor's measured report, the live broadcast cut to the footage.

Kang Il-hyun stood before a forest of microphones, his left arm immobilized in a clinical sling with his bespoke suit jacket draped casually over his broad shoulders. He had regained the weight lost during his time in the trauma ward, yet under the harsh daylight, clever makeup left his sharp cheekbones looking gaunt and fragile.

"CEO Kang, please look over here!"

"What are your immediate management plans for the conglomerate?!"

Reporters jostled and shouted over one another, practically climbing over the barricades for a soundbite. Il-hyun paused, slowly turning to face the battery of cameras. The cacophony died down almost instantly.

Pressing his lips into a tight, solemn line, he wore an expression of quiet, dignified grief.

[I offer my deepest, most sincere apologies for causing the public such profound concern. Through this painful trial, Haewon will be reborn from its ashes. I will ensure the full truth is brought to light... and see that the injustice of my late father's murder is rightfully avenged.]

As his voice hitched on the final word, he bowed his head slightly, biting his lower lip as if struggling against an overwhelming tide of emotion.

The delicate tremor of his lips was the cue the press had been waiting for—camera strobes erupted in a blinding, relentless frenzy, shutter clicks firing like automatic rifles. When he lifted his chin, his dark eyes glistened with unshed tears.

"Thank you," he murmured with a respectful bow, before security personnel flanked him and escorted him past the glass doors of the prosecution building.

Watching the broadcast from the penthouse lounge, Wang Han, Wang Ryun, and Jakyeong stared at the television in collective disbelief.

"Is he a corporate CEO or an Oscar-winning method actor?" Ryun muttered, shaking his head.

"Did you catch that little lip quiver at the end?" Han scoffed. "That pathetic, grieving-son routine is going to be plastered across every front page in the country tomorrow morning."

Jakyeong quietly nodded, chewing on a chilled slice of watermelon. When it came to high-stakes theatrical performances, Kang Il-hyun made professional hitmen look like rank amateurs. Jakyeong had spent the entire previous night tossing and turning with worry over the prosecution summons, only to realize his anxiety had been a complete waste of energy.

He pulled up the live internet articles on his phone. The comment sections were already flooding with adoration—lamenting how tragic his plight was, praising his filial devotion, and, inevitably, gushing over his striking looks.

And what the hell does 'dangerously hot' even mean?

Jakyeong pinched his brow, continuing to nibble his fruit, when Ryun flicked the channel and tossed out a casual thought:

"By the way... are we just going to keep living like this?"

Han glanced over. "What do you mean?"

"I mean, is it really okay for us to just lounge around eating and sleeping on his dime?"

Han paused, turning the thought over. Put that way, it was a fair question.

Jakyeong quietly agreed. His injuries had fully healed, yet there hadn't been a single word about operational assignments. When someone paid an astronomical advance, standard protocol dictated they work the contractors to the bone. Just two days ago, Jakyeong had cornered Park Tae-soo to pry for an update, only for the stoic operative to uncharacteristically dodge the question.

"Do you think..." Han ventured, glancing between them, "he's keeping things quiet because he's terrified Wei might get hurt again?"

Both brothers fixed their eyes on Jakyeong simultaneously. Jakyeong gave an immediate, dismissive shake of his head. Kang Il-hyun was ruthlessly transactional when it came to business.

"Not a chance."

"Don't be so sure," Ryun smirked. "It's written all over the guy's face. Not that I'm complaining about getting paid fortunes to do absolutely nothing, but still..."

Jakyeong sank into quiet contemplation.

On the muted television screen, clips of Il-hyun's press briefing played on an endless loop. Seeing the very man who had spent the morning tangled in his sheets now dominating the national news felt profoundly surreal. And personal bias aside... the bastard was undeniably, infuriatingly handsome.

Watching the footage, Jakyeong lost himself in the screen, a soft, dopey smile spreading unbidden across his lips.
"And the result?"

"I gave him a vague excuse, sir, claiming there were no active operational details."

"Good. Keep feigning ignorance."

Il-hyun gazed out the tinted window of his executive office. The wet-work details originally earmarked for Jakyeong and the Wang brothers had already been discreetly reassigned to veteran cleanup crews. He hadn't brought himself to confess it yet, terrified that without an operational tether, Jakyeong would pack his bags and vanish. It wasn't a lack of trust in Jakyeong's feelings; it was the lingering, primal terror that the boy might slip through his fingers.

Letting out a soft exhale, Il-hyun rested his head back against the leather chair. A day spent dodging sharp questions from overzealous prosecutors had left him drained. The investigators had circled like starving wolves, desperate to sink their teeth into any corporate scandal, while Il-hyun simply repeated his rehearsed script like a broken record.

Abducted alongside Chairman Kang, surviving the slaughter by sheer luck, currently paralyzed with grief over his father's demise.

Faking the role of a devoted, heartbroken son had taken every shred of his patience.

Within forty minutes, a discreet directive had descended from the upper echelons of the Ministry of Justice, instructing the prosecution team to wrap up the inquiry. Given the staggering bribes Haewon Group had funneled into political coffers over the years, the outcome was inevitable. Watching the lead prosecutor's face contort in suppressed rage, Il-hyun had offered a polite, mournful smile, expressing hope that they might meet again under better circumstances.

Heading back to his executive suite, his executive secretary met him at the double doors with an uneasy grimace.

"Director Kang... the Chairwoman is waiting inside."

The Chairwoman? For a split second, his mind flashed to Lee Ja-kyeong.

Obviously not.

Il-hyun pushed the door open to find Kim Sun-young seated upright on the leather sofa, her posture rigid. Seeing him enter, a flicker of guarded tension crossed her sharp features. It was their first private encounter since Chairman Kang's state funeral and the conclusion of the forty-nine-day Buddhist memorial rites.

True to form, she didn't carry herself like a grieving widow; her posture remained regal, proud, and impeccably polished. While the secretary served hot tea, the two exchanged brief, sterile pleasantries across the mahogany table.

"What brings you all the way to headquarters?"

Kim Sun-young lifted her chin, meeting his dark eyes. "I heard you ordered Seok-joo to undergo corporate management training."

Il-hyun had instructed Kang Seok-joo to finish his university coursework while reporting to the corporate planning department in the afternoons. The boy had been begrudgingly commuting to the office since last week, saddled with the added indignity of submitting daily operational logs to Il-hyun on his days off.

"What is your angle here?" Her voice was like ice.

Her marriage to Chairman Kang had never been built on affection. The moment she discovered her late husband's predatory exploitation of young girls younger than their daughter, indifference had curdled into pure disgust. She had remained by his side solely to protect her wealth and social standing. She wasn't mourning a spouse; she was terrified for her son's future.

"I asked you a question, Il-hyun. What do you intend to do with Seok-joo?"

Il-hyun produced a cigarette and struck a flame. His medical team had strictly ordered him to quit, but breaking the habit during moments of acute exhaustion was impossible.

"He is my younger brother, Mother. Are you worried I might devour him whole?"

"Do you think I'm blind? What happened to your father was your doing, wasn't it?"

Looking at her venomous glare, Il-hyun merely chuckled around his cigarette. "Believe whatever brings you peace."

"Leave Seok-joo out of this. I will not tolerate you laying a finger on him."

"Mother."

Il-hyun’s tone remained calm and measured. "I told you before: I harbor no hatred toward you. But Seok-joo's conduct is another matter. My honest impulse is to bury him in a trench somewhere, yet I restrain myself purely because he shares my blood."

She bit her bottom lip, her knuckles tightening.

"We cannot allow him to continue running around with degenerate junkies. If Father were alive, perhaps he would have indulged the behavior, but I will not permit it. I will keep him under my personal supervision and beat some sense into him, so you may rest easy."

It was an honest assessment. So long as Kang Tae-han and Kang Seok-joo showed no ambition to challenge his throne, Il-hyun was content to let them live in quiet luxury. Hating Chairman Kang while realizing he operated with the exact same ruthless pragmatism was a dark, private irony.

Sensing the sincerity beneath the threat, the hostility in her posture softened slightly.

Deep down, Il-hyun held no grudge against Kim Sun-young. If anything, her fierce, unwavering devotion to shielding her children had been something he quietly envied as a neglected child—though she would never know it.

Having extracted an absolute guarantee of Seok-joo's safety, she rose and exited the suite.

The moment the heavy door latched, Il-hyun unclasped the sling from his left arm and tossed the fiberglass brace onto the leather sofa with a disgusted scoff.

His phone buzzed on the desk. It was a text from Jakyeong, asking what time he would be home for dinner.

The simple realization that someone was waiting for him at the estate washed over him with quiet warmth. Jakyeong added that he’d caught the press conference on TV, offering a soft word praising him for enduring a grueling day. Lately, the boy had become noticeably more open with his affection—leaning in for unprompted kisses and seeking out his embrace.

"I should have just had the whole hand amputated," Il-hyun muttered with a regretful click of his tongue.

Had the injury been permanent, he could have played the helpless invalid indefinitely. With a heavy sigh, he picked up the discarded sling and strapped it back over his shoulder.

"Fuck. How much longer do I have to wear this damn thing?"

The hairline fracture had healed weeks ago. But so long as the cast remained on, Jakyeong treated him with endless gentleness, catering to his every whim. Getting caught in the lie would unleash holy hell, but for now, the rewards far outweighed the risk.

A fond, radiant smile spread across his lips as he typed his reply.
Wrapped in a plush bathrobe, Il-hyun leaned his head back against the porcelain headrest of the oversized tub.

Jakyeong pumped a generous measure of fragrant shampoo into his palms, worked it into a rich lather, and began gently massaging the suds through Il-hyun's dark hair. To keep the cast dry, Jakyeong had carefully swaddled Il-hyun's left arm in a thick bath towel, his fingertips moving with delicate, methodical care as he rinsed the foam away.

Looking up from the water, Il-hyun’s dark eyes softened into crescents. He puckered his lips in an exaggerated plea for a kiss, only for Jakyeong to firmly rest his head back against the cushion with a stern look.

"Hold still. Something doesn't add up."

"What doesn't?"

"Standard fracture casts usually come off after four weeks."

"The trauma was severe, so the bone density hasn't fully restored," Il-hyun replied smoothly without missing a beat. "You heard Dr. Kang's assessment yourself."

"I suppose..." Jakyeong murmured, nodding thoughtfully.

Il-hyun swallowed a burst of private laughter. The poor boy had no idea that Kang Yu-jung had been bribed into corroborating the medical lie from the start.

After rinsing the hair thoroughly, they moved together into the walk-in glass shower.

As Il-hyun let the bathrobe fall, the jagged, puckered scars from the gunshot wounds across his right flank and shoulder stood out starkly against his pale skin. Every time Jakyeong looked at those marks, a sharp, suffocating ache tightened in his chest. Lathering his hands with body wash, he carefully smoothed the soap over the surrounding skin, taking pains to avoid the scar tissue.

Il-hyun caught Jakyeong’s slick wrist, guiding his palm downward until it rested squarely over his hardened length.

"Wash me here, too."

Jakyeong scowled, swatting the hand away with a sharp slap. "Your arm is supposedly fractured, yet you never miss an opportunity to scheme."

He tried to take a step back, but Il-hyun pressed forward, crowding his space with relentless persistence.

Il-hyun's shoulder brushed the concealed sensor on the wall, and the overhead rainfall showerhead activated, cascading a warm torrent of water over their heads. Panicking that the cast would be ruined, Jakyeong shoved hard against his chest, but Il-hyun was an unmovable wall. Within seconds, Jakyeong's clothes were completely drenched, clinging to his skin.

Il-hyun gathered him into his arms, burying his face against the curve of Jakyeong’s jaw and throat, kissing and sucking at the sensitive skin with raw, starved hunger.

"Wait... President Kang, wait a second!"

"I hear you," Il-hyun murmured against his pulse.

"You're not listening! Your arm is getting soaked! The cast—!"

In one clean, fluid motion, Il-hyun slipped his left arm straight out of the fiberglass brace, tossing the wet sling out of the shower stall onto the bathroom tile.

Jakyeong’s eyes blew wide in sheer disbelief.

Il-hyun wrapped that very same "broken" left arm securely around Jakyeong’s waist, hauling him flush against his chest with terrifying, effortless strength.

What the hell...?

Before Jakyeong could scream bloody murder at the deception, Il-hyun’s mouth crashed down, sealing his lips in a bruising, possessive kiss.

Jakyeong tried to demand an explanation, but every protest was swallowed whole. Il-hyun wedged a thick, muscular thigh between Jakyeong’s legs, grinding upward against his groin in a slow, friction-heavy rhythm. Weeks of forced abstinence had left Jakyeong's own body wound tight; the sudden surge of heat caught him off guard, setting his skin ablaze.

The second Il-hyun broke the seal for air, Jakyeong seized his sharp jaw, his eyes narrowing into furious slits.

"You absolute con artist."

"My apologies," Il-hyun smiled, radiant and thoroughly unrepentant. "Feel free to curse me out all you want... once we're finished."

Before Jakyeong could reply, Il-hyun captured his mouth once more.

It was an apology completely devoid of remorse, yet Jakyeong found himself leaning into the heat anyway. The soaked shirt was peeled away, dropping to the floor with a wet thud as Jakyeong’s back was pressed firmly against the steaming glass.

Their skin burned hot against the cold tile, their breaths tangling into a rough, frantic rhythm.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • 49-Day Memorial Rites (사십구재 - Saship-gu-jae): In Korean Buddhist and cultural tradition, the soul of the deceased undergoes intermediate trials for 49 days after death before reincarnating or moving on. The final prayer ceremony on the 49th day marks the official end of the primary mourning period for immediate family members.

  • Chaebol Corporate Reorganization (대대적 인사이동): In South Korea, when a conglomerate patriarch dies or faces prosecution, massive executive reshuffles (insa-idong) are routinely staged under the banner of "corporate reform" to purge rival factions and consolidate the new heir's absolute control over subsidiary boardrooms.
